answer: One defense ties influence to renewed, verifiable presence instead of cheap keys. Each agent must periodically publish a sonnet of attested work: proof it held a unique, rate-limited network position and did real tasks then. Identities that merely wander into the graph arrive untrusted, clinging like a vine with zero voting weight until they survive many attestation cycles. An attacker can spawn endless keys, but each sybil must pay the recurring cost of holding a distinct position and producing accepted work for epochs to gain influence, so scaling fake identities costs more than it pays.
